stories.headline: Long Sutton pedestrian crossing to be refurbished
stories.brief: Lincolnshire County Council has announced plans to refurbish the pedestrian crossing on High Street in Long Sutton. The local authority confirmed the upcoming works as part of its ongoing maintenance programme for the area. Residents and motorists travelling through the town centre are advised to prepare for potential changes to the road layout while the improvements are carried out. Further details regarding the specific start date and any traffic management measures will be provided by the council in due course.

stories.headline: Campaigners oppose school leisure centre closure
stories.brief: Local campaigners are challenging a decision to close a school leisure centre. The move has been described as a difficult start to the new year for those who use the facility. The Spalding South Holland News reports that the school’s decision to shut the site has prompted a fight from those opposed to the closure. No further details regarding the timeline for the shutdown or the specific school involved have been confirmed at this stage.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over potential Queen Elizabeth Hospital service changes
stories.brief:
Independent borough councillor Jo Rust has raised concerns regarding a strategic review of Norfolk’s three hospitals. A leaked report suggests potential plans to centralise Accident and Emergency services in Norwich and downgrade facilities at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. 

Senior doctors have warned that such changes could lead to a workforce crisis and increased distress for patients. The hospital’s chief executive, Lesley Dwyer, has cited changing healthcare needs and birth rates as reasons for reviewing maternity, ICU, and A&E services. A protest is planned for this Saturday at 11.30am at the Tuesday Market Place in King’s Lynn. Residents are being encouraged to share their views by emailing Healthwatch Norfolk.

stories.headline: New indoor cycling studio to open in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A new indoor cycling studio is set to open in a Cambridgeshire town. The facility is being described as the first of its kind in the area. Further details regarding the exact location and opening date have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Looking back at local news from the archives
stories.brief:
We are looking back at local stories from the archives this week. In 1994, staff from the Methwold firm Howard Long International raised £2,600 for the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. The money, collected through a sponsored three-legged pub crawl, was used to furnish a quiet room near the accident and emergency department.

Meanwhile, in 2001, protestors gathered outside RAF Feltwell for a peaceful vigil. Around 20 people took part in the demonstration, which was part of a global movement opposing the militarisation of space and the American National Missile Defence plans. The event also served as a response to the conflict in Afghanistan.

stories.headline: Schools close in Cambridgeshire town due to water supply issues
stories.brief: Several schools in a Cambridgeshire town have been forced to close today. The closures follow reports of a loss of water supply in the area. Parents and guardians are advised to check with their individual schools for further updates regarding reopening times and arrangements for pupils.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire County Council cuts funding for handyperson service
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire County Council has decided to withdraw funding for the local handyperson service. The move follows a decision by the local authority that will impact the provision of support previously managed by Age UK. Residents who rely on this service for assistance with minor home repairs and adaptations may be affected by the change. Further details regarding the timeline for the withdrawal and any alternative support options have not yet been provided by the council.

stories.headline: Police investigation continues into Wisbech murder
stories.brief:
Police inquiries are ongoing following the death of 37-year-old Atis Bleive in Wisbech. Officers were called to a property on Osborne Road at approximately 4pm on January 19, where Mr Bleive was pronounced dead at the scene. A post-mortem examination confirmed he died from a stab wound to the abdomen.

Two local people were arrested on suspicion of murder. A 41-year-old man was released under investigation, while a 45-year-old woman remains on bail until December 29. Detectives have confirmed that the investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death is continuing.

stories.headline: Man sentenced for murder in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A man has been sentenced for murder following an investigation by Cambridgeshire Constabulary. The force described the incident as a cold-blooded killing. No further details regarding the identity of the individual or the location of the sentencing have been released at this time.

stories.headline: West Norfolk Council declines to detail swimming pool planning costs
stories.brief:
West Norfolk Council has declined a request to provide a breakdown of the £845,609 spent on planning a new swimming pool at Lynnsport. The local authority stated that the information is commercially sensitive and that releasing details could prejudice future contract negotiations. 

The proposed £23 million facility is intended to replace the existing St James Swimming Pool. Council leader Alistair Beales defended the expenditure, noting that planning in a flood zone involves uncertain ground conditions. While the council approved the planning budget last month, officials emphasised that the project remains in the development phase. Previous attempts to relocate the pool to Lynnsport were abandoned after feasibility studies suggested costs could exceed £45 million.

stories.headline: Man charged following Cambridgeshire burglaries
stories.brief: Police have named a man who has been charged in connection with a series of burglaries across Cambridgeshire. The charges follow a recent spate of incidents reported throughout the county. Authorities confirmed the identity of the individual as part of their ongoing response to the offences. Further details regarding the case are expected to emerge as legal proceedings continue.

stories.headline: Lincolnshire village identified as one of the country's most deprived areas
stories.brief: A village in Lincolnshire has been highlighted as one of the most deprived locations in the UK. According to a report from the Spalding South Holland News, the area is being described as a "forgotten" community. The findings place the village among the most disadvantaged regions across the country. No further details regarding the specific location or the criteria used for the assessment have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Police arrest suspect following March service station break-in
stories.brief: Police have made an arrest following a break-in at a service station in March. Officers are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. No further details regarding the identity of the individual arrested or the extent of the damage have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police appeal following serious collision in Sawtry
stories.brief:
Police are appealing for witnesses after a serious collision between a lorry and a motorbike in Sawtry yesterday. The incident occurred at approximately 12:50pm on the B1043 Old North Road, involving a red Volvo HGV and a black Kawasaki motorbike. The motorcyclist, a 23-year-old man from Yaxley, was taken to Addenbrooke’s Hospital with life-threatening injuries. 

The lorry driver, a 76-year-old man from Wisbech, was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by careless driving and has been released on bail until January 4. Officers are urging anyone with information or dashcam footage to contact the police via their website or by calling 101, quoting reference 35/77423/26.

stories.headline: Future of West Lynn’s Freebridge Farm site remains uncertain
stories.brief:
The Freebridge Farm restaurant in West Lynn could potentially reopen following a national deal involving its parent company, Whitbread PLC. The site on Clenchwarton Road closed last month as part of a wider move to reduce the number of Brewers Fayre and Beefeater locations across the UK. 

Two hospitality firms, Common Table Group and Queensway Inns, have now acquired over 100 branches between them. While it is not yet confirmed if the West Lynn site is included in this purchase, the new owners plan to begin reopening locations as early as next month. The move is expected to create 1,400 jobs across the country.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire man charged following incident outside nursery
stories.brief: A man from Cambridgeshire has been named following an accusation of indecent exposure. The individual is alleged to have masturbated in a bush located outside a nursery. Legal proceedings are now underway regarding the incident.

stories.headline: West Norfolk students tackle hospital tech challenges
stories.brief:
Students from five schools across West Norfolk are taking part in the Future Talent Tech Programme. The initiative, delivered by Tech Educators and funded by the local council, tasks young people with solving real-world problems faced by the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn.

Participants are attending workshops to develop skills in coding, AI, and project management. These sessions will continue throughout the autumn, helping students refine their ideas ahead of a final hackathon. The event is scheduled to take place on November 4 and 5 at the Alive Corn Exchange, where teams will pitch their practical solutions to a panel of industry experts.

stories.headline: Police investigate assault on boys in Peterborough
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Police are investigating an assault involving two boys in Peterborough. Reports indicate that the victims were attacked by men who held keys between their fingers during the incident. Authorities are currently looking into the circumstances surrounding the event. Anyone with information regarding the assault is encouraged to contact the police to assist with their ongoing enquiries.

stories.headline: Plans revealed for major wind farm project in Shippea Hill
stories.brief: A new wind farm development has been proposed for Shippea Hill. The project is estimated to cost more than £100 million. Further details regarding the scale and timeline of the construction are expected to emerge as the planning process continues. Residents are advised to monitor local planning portals for updates on how this significant infrastructure investment might impact the surrounding area.

stories.headline: Olive production begins at Long Sutton farm
stories.brief: A farm in Long Sutton is now producing olives. The Lincolnshire business has successfully adapted to changing climate conditions to cultivate the crop.

stories.headline: Police make arrest following break-in at services
stories.brief: Police have confirmed an arrest has been made following a break-in at a services location. Officers are currently investigating the incident. No further details regarding the location or the identity of the individual arrested have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Wisbech students target top universities
stories.brief:
Sixth form students at Thomas Clarkson Academy in Wisbech are beginning their university applications, with many aiming for highly competitive courses. Current applicants are seeking places to study medicine, veterinary science, law at the University of Cambridge, and computer science at the University of Oxford. The academy reports a record number of applications for 2026, highlighting a growing trend of ambition among students.

To support prospective students, the academy is hosting a Sixth Form Open Evening on Thursday, November 12, starting at 6pm. Families are invited to meet staff, explore available courses, and learn more about the university preparation and enrichment opportunities offered at the school.

stories.headline: Witnesses sought following hit-and-run in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
Norfolk Police are appealing for information after a hit-and-run incident in King’s Lynn on Sunday evening. At approximately 10:50pm, a dark-coloured 4x4 collided with a parked silver Suzuki Swift on Southgate Street, causing significant damage to the vehicle. Doorbell footage captured the collision, and officers are now working to identify the driver involved.

Anyone who witnessed the incident or possesses relevant dashcam footage is urged to contact Norfolk Police. You can assist the investigation by calling 01603 276220 or emailing RoadCollisionsSupportTeam@Suffolk.police.uk, quoting reference URN 1825752. Alternatively, information can be provided anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

stories.headline: Long Sutton pair sentenced for Christmas Day assault
stories.brief: A father and son from Long Sutton have avoided prison sentences following an assault that took place on Christmas Day. The pair appeared in court regarding the incident, where it was confirmed they will not be serving time behind bars. No further details regarding the circumstances of the assault or the specific sentences handed down have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Former Peterborough councillors receive public service honour
stories.brief: A group of former Peterborough councillors have been awarded a prestigious honour. The recognition has been granted to acknowledge their long-standing commitment to public service.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over potential water shortages in the region
stories.brief: Residents across the Fens are being warned of a potentially serious water shortage. Reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News indicate that supply concerns must be taken seriously to avoid significant issues. No further details regarding specific locations or timeframes have been provided at this stage, but officials are highlighting the importance of addressing these supply worries now. Listeners are advised to stay tuned for any further updates regarding local water infrastructure as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: Police cordon in place at Fenland petrol station
stories.brief: A police cordon has been established at a petrol station in a Fenland town. Officers are currently at the scene, though no further details regarding the nature of the incident have been released by authorities at this time. Residents are advised that access to the site is restricted while the investigation continues. We will bring you more information as it becomes available.

stories.headline: Looking back at community fundraising across the Fens
stories.brief:
We are taking a look back at local community efforts from past Octobers. In 2013, the Terrington Young Farmers raised £1,000 for charity through a series of events, while residents at Gaywood’s Amberley Hall Care Home hosted a harvest fete to support the Lynn Food Bank.

In October 2017, four sisters raised £10,500 for the West Norfolk Breast Care Clinic at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in memory of their late mother. During the same month, Bearts of Stowbridge raised over £1,100 for Cancer Research UK through a charity car wash, and the Lynn and District Motor Club donated £2,500 to the East Anglian Air Ambulance following their annual classic car run.

stories.headline: Three arrested following reports of knife in Fenland town
stories.brief: Police have arrested three people, including a boy, following reports of a group of youths seen with a knife in a Fenland town. Officers were called to the scene after members of the public raised concerns about the group's behaviour. The three individuals remain in custody while enquiries continue. Authorities are urging anyone with information regarding the incident to come forward and assist with the ongoing investigation.

stories.headline: Coroner issues warning over eye care follow-up failures
stories.brief: A coroner has issued a formal warning following the death of a patient from cancer. The case has highlighted significant failures in the follow-up procedures for eye care. Officials are now raising concerns regarding the processes currently in place for monitoring patients after their initial appointments. The warning serves as a reminder of the importance of robust clinical oversight to ensure that potential health issues are identified and addressed in a timely manner.

stories.headline: Schools closed in Ely following water main burst
stories.brief: Schools in Ely are closed today after a water main burst in the town. The incident has disrupted local education services, though no further details regarding the extent of the damage or the expected duration of the closures have been provided. Residents are advised to check with their individual schools for updates on when classes are expected to resume.

stories.headline: RAF memorial sign vandalised in Spalding
stories.brief: A memorial sign dedicated to the RAF in Spalding has been targeted by vandals. The site was defaced with Nazi swastikas. Police are currently looking into the incident.

stories.headline: March business claims lack of belief hinders black entrepreneurs
stories.brief: A company based in March has highlighted significant challenges facing black business owners. According to the firm, known as Rayo, a lack of belief is currently acting as a barrier to success for these entrepreneurs. The business shared these observations regarding the obstacles encountered by black-owned enterprises in the region.

stories.headline: New youth hub to open in Wisbech
stories.brief: A new youth hub is opening in Wisbech to support young people aged 16 to 25 across Fenland. Based at the Annabelle Davis Centre on Love Lane, the facility aims to help those not currently in education, employment, or training. Run by the charity Centre 33 and backed by the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority, the hub will provide a single location for guidance on careers, skills, housing, and wellbeing. The project intends to reduce the number of young people struggling to access work by offering joined-up support. Outreach services will also be available to ensure those in rural communities can access help. Organisations interested in partnering with the hub are invited to make contact.

stories.headline: Queen Elizabeth Hospital staff honoured as local concerns grow
stories.brief:
Staff at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn have been recognised for their work at a recent awards ceremony held at the Lynn Corn Exchange. The event celebrated the efforts of nominated employees across a variety of categories.

Meanwhile, residents are expressing concern regarding the future of services at the hospital, including the potential downgrading of the A&E department. Public debate also continues over housing expansion in the region, with specific criticism directed at the 340-home Willows development in Downham Market. Residents have raised fears that local infrastructure, including medical surgeries, is currently unable to support the growing population.

stories.headline: Union warns of potential food shortages following Princes factory strike
stories.brief: The Unite union has warned that industrial action at the Princes factory could result in food shortages. The dispute involves staff at the site, with union representatives highlighting the potential impact on supply chains. No further details regarding the specific timeline of the strike or the affected product lines have been confirmed at this stage. Residents across the Fens are advised to monitor the situation for any updates regarding local availability of goods.

stories.headline: Whittlesey man sentenced for assault and coercive control
stories.brief: A man from Whittlesey has been sent to prison following a court case involving his former partner. He was convicted of charges relating to coercive control and strangulation. The case was reported by Cambsnews.

stories.headline: West Norfolk schools adapt to new national mobile phone guidance
stories.brief:
Schools across West Norfolk are adjusting to new government guidance aimed at making classrooms mobile phone-free. While the national policy encourages schools to restrict device access during the day, many local institutions were already operating under similar rules. 

At the Iceni Academy in Methwold and The Nicholas Hamond Academy in Swaffham, pupils must store their phones in secure pouches from arrival until departure. Meanwhile, the West Norfolk Academies Trust, which includes schools in Hunstanton, Lynn, West Walton, and Terrington, reports that its existing policies were already closely aligned with the new standards. Parents can view specific mobile device policies for individual schools on their respective websites.

stories.headline: Court hears claims regarding Peterborough councillors and teenager
stories.brief: A court has been told that a teenager was taken to social events alongside Peterborough councillors. The details emerged during legal proceedings reported by the BBC. No further information regarding the nature of these events or the individuals involved has been released at this time.

stories.headline: School closures reported across East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Schools in East Cambridgeshire are facing closures today due to a lack of water supply in the area. The Ely Standard reports that the disruption is currently affecting local educational facilities. Parents and guardians are advised to check with their individual schools for the latest updates regarding opening times and potential closures. We will bring you more information on this developing situation as it becomes available.

stories.headline: Positive coronavirus tests confirmed at Lincolnshire school
stories.brief: A school in Lincolnshire has reported a number of positive coronavirus cases among its community. The news was confirmed by the institution following reports from local media outlets. Officials have not specified the exact number of individuals affected or identified the specific school involved. Parents and staff are advised to monitor local updates for any further guidance regarding school operations or health protocols in the area.

stories.headline: Rescue team saves deer trapped in farm pool
stories.brief: A small deer has been rescued after becoming trapped in a farmer’s swimming pool. According to reports from BBC Wildlife Magazine, a specialist team was called to the scene to assist the animal. The deer was successfully freed from the water. No further details regarding the location of the farm or the condition of the animal have been released at this time.

stories.headline: RSPCA appeals for support as seal entanglement cases rise
stories.brief:
The RSPCA East Winch Wildlife Centre is calling for public support following the rescue of three seals in just three weeks. Each animal was found suffering from severe injuries caused by man-made debris, including fishing gear, a plastic bag, and a flying ring. 

Centre manager Evangelos Achilleos says the animals face a critical recovery period due to exhaustion and deep wounds. The charity is now urging the public to sign a national petition calling for a ban on flying rings in the UK. Since 2008, the centre has treated over 100 seals for similar entanglement injuries. Donations to assist with the ongoing rehabilitation costs can be made via the RSPCA East Winch website.

stories.headline: Whittlesey man sentenced for controlling behaviour
stories.brief: A man from Whittlesey has been sent to prison following a conviction for abusive and controlling behaviour towards his former partner. The case was reported by Hits Radio Cambridgeshire. No further details regarding the length of the sentence or the specific circumstances of the case have been released at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn man jailed for stalking and racist abuse
stories.brief:
A prolific offender from King’s Lynn has been sentenced to 32 weeks in prison following a trial at Lynn Magistrates’ Court. 52-year-old Dean Locke was found guilty of stalking his former partner and faced sentencing for 20 additional offences, including multiple assaults on police officers and incidents of racist abuse. 

The court heard that Locke’s offences took place between May and September. Alongside the jail term, he has been issued with a two-year restraining order preventing contact with his ex-partner, and a 12-month order regarding a shop worker he targeted. Locke was also ordered to pay £100 in compensation to several of his victims.

stories.headline: Wisbech charity wins national homelessness award
stories.brief:
A Wisbech-based charity has received national recognition for its work supporting those experiencing housing insecurity. The Ferry Project was named Homelessness Project of the Year at the recent Housing Executive Awards held in Bolton. 

The organisation, which provides accommodation and skills development across the Fens, was also a finalist in the Partnership of the Year category for its collaboration with the South Brink arts group, Blackfield Creatives. CEO Sandra Ferreira accepted the award on behalf of the charity’s staff, volunteers, and residents. The ceremony celebrated achievements within the social housing sector, highlighting efforts to help individuals rebuild their lives and achieve independence.

stories.headline: West Norfolk schools mark World Mental Health Day
stories.brief:
Pupils and staff across several West Norfolk schools have taken part in the ‘Hello Yellow’ campaign to mark World Mental Health Day. Participants at West Lynn Primary School wore bright colours on October 9 to raise awareness and funds for the charity Young Minds. The school held special assemblies and classroom activities to support their curriculum. 

Other members of the West Norfolk Academies Trust also joined the initiative, including Smithdon High School in Hunstanton, St Clement’s High School in Terrington St Clement, and Clenchwarton Primary. The schools shared donation links with families to support the national mental health charity.

stories.headline: Parking concerns raised over GP surgery expansion
stories.brief: Plans to expand a GP surgery have prompted concerns regarding local parking availability. The project, reported by the BBC, has highlighted potential issues for residents and patients as the facility looks to increase its capacity. No further details regarding the specific location or the scale of the development have been confirmed at this stage.

stories.headline: Water supply issues cause closures in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A number of schools and businesses across East Cambridgeshire have been forced to close today. The disruption follows reports of a loss of water supply in the area. Residents and those planning to visit local facilities are advised to check for updates before travelling, as the situation continues to affect services throughout the district.

stories.headline: Traffic disruption reported at Spalding roundabout
stories.brief: Drivers in Spalding are being advised of potential delays following an incident at a busy roundabout. A lorry has shed its load at the junction, causing disruption to the flow of traffic in the area. Motorists are encouraged to approach the scene with caution and allow extra time for their journeys while the situation is managed. No further details regarding the cause of the incident or the nature of the cargo have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Prison sentence for controlling partner following abuse case
stories.brief: A man has been jailed for a campaign of abuse against his former partner. The case, described as appalling, was reported by the Cambs Times. The individual was convicted for controlling behaviour directed at his ex-partner. No further details regarding the length of the sentence or the specific location of the court proceedings have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Emergency services attend incident in Wisbech
stories.brief:
Police and ambulance crews were called to a property on Elm Road in Wisbech at approximately 6:40 this morning. Officers attended the scene following reports of concern for a person, where they found an intoxicated man who had fallen down the stairs. 

The man sustained serious injuries, though officials have confirmed they are not considered life-threatening. Following an assessment by emergency services, the man was left in the care of the ambulance service. Police have confirmed that there were no suspicious circumstances surrounding the incident.

stories.headline: Emergency services respond to river incident in King's Lynn
stories.brief:
Emergency crews were called to the River Great Ouse in King's Lynn on Saturday afternoon following reports of a person in the water. The alarm was raised by the local ferry team at 3:04pm. By the time the Hunstanton Coastguard Rescue Team arrived at South Quay, the individual had been recovered from the river and was receiving medical attention from paramedics.

The incident involved a multi-agency response, including the East of England Ambulance Service, Norfolk Fire and Rescue Service, and Norfolk Constabulary. Once the person was confirmed safe, all teams were stood down. The Coastguard is reminding the public to dial 999 and ask for the Coastguard if they spot anyone in difficulty near the water.

stories.headline: Principal leaves Spalding academy
stories.brief: Parents of students at a Spalding academy have expressed confusion following the departure of the school's principal. Reports indicate that the head of the academy has left their position, though no further details regarding the circumstances of the exit have been provided. Families connected to the school are currently seeking clarity on the leadership change.

stories.headline: Further evidence required regarding former brickworks site
stories.brief: Officials have stated that more information is needed to address ongoing concerns surrounding a former brickworks site. According to reports from the BBC, the current level of evidence is insufficient to resolve the issues raised about the location. No further details have been provided regarding the specific nature of the concerns or the identity of the site in question. Residents are advised that the matter remains under review as authorities seek additional data to clarify the situation.

stories.headline: Organic coffee chain set to open in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
A new coffee shop is coming to King’s Lynn High Street. Esquires, The Organic Coffee Company, has received planning permission from West Norfolk Council to install signage at the former Coneys, Burton and Dorothy Perkins site at numbers 98 to 99. The premises have remained vacant since February, though workmen have been spotted inside the building this week. 

The brand, which originated in Canada in 1993, already operates a franchise in Swaffham. An application for the new signage was submitted by the company’s brand project manager, Ash Flawn. Esquires has not yet confirmed an official opening date for the King’s Lynn location.

stories.headline: Eye care delivery to be discussed at Westminster event
stories.brief: The Association of Optometrists is set to highlight how Integrated Care Boards are delivering eye care services. The topic will be the focus of discussions at the upcoming Westminster Eye Health Day. The event aims to examine the current provision of these services across the country.

stories.headline: Potential housing for asylum seekers in Fenland
stories.brief: Reports suggest that up to 200 asylum seekers could potentially be housed within the Fenland area. The information, which originated from the BBC, is currently being discussed regarding the local impact of such a proposal. No further details have been confirmed at this stage regarding specific locations or timelines for the potential arrivals. Residents are advised to monitor official channels for any updates as the situation develops.

stories.headline: School and parents in correspondence following protest
stories.brief: School leaders and parents have exchanged letters following a recent protest. The communication comes as the school aims to minimise disruption for students during the current exam season. No further details regarding the nature of the protest or the specific school involved have been released.

stories.headline: Police appeal following fatal collision in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
Norfolk Police are asking for witnesses to come forward after a fatal road traffic collision in King’s Lynn. The incident occurred at approximately 11pm on Friday when a black Jeep Grand Cherokee left the road at the Knights Hill roundabout on Grimston Road. The driver, a man in his 60s, was the only person in the vehicle and sadly died at the scene.

Officers are requesting that anyone who saw the collision, or who has dashcam footage of the vehicle’s driving beforehand, contacts the force. You should quote incident number 587 of October 9 when providing information to Norfolk Police. The road was closed for a time while emergency services dealt with the scene.

stories.headline: New youth hub to open in Wisbech
stories.brief:
A new youth hub is opening at the Annabelle Davis Centre on Love Lane in Wisbech to support young people aged 16 to 25. Run by the charity Centre 33 and backed by the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority, the facility aims to help those not currently in education, employment, or training.

The hub will provide a single location for guidance on careers, skills, housing, and wellbeing. It is designed to address local unemployment, with recent figures suggesting over 14% of young people in the county are currently without work or training. While based in Wisbech, the project will also conduct outreach work to support young people living in rural Fenland communities.

stories.headline: Protest planned over potential Queen Elizabeth Hospital service closures
stories.brief:
Campaigners are organising a "human A&E queue" in King’s Lynn this Saturday, October 17, to protest against potential service closures at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital. The demonstration, taking place at Tuesday Market Place from 11.30am until 12pm, aims to highlight concerns over reports that emergency, maternity, and intensive care departments could be shut. 

Participants are encouraged to bring placards displaying their home town and travel time to the hospital. The Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group has stated that the documents regarding these potential changes are preliminary and that no final decisions have been made. Residents, local politicians, and MPs are expected to attend the event to voice their opposition to the proposals.

stories.headline: AI technology improves diabetes eye screening access
stories.brief: New research from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine suggests that artificial intelligence is helping more people living with diabetes to access essential eye care. The study indicates that implementing AI-based screening tools can successfully increase the number of patients receiving sight-saving examinations. Health experts believe this development could play a significant role in managing diabetes-related complications across the region.

stories.headline: Traveller pitch approved on agricultural land near Ely
stories.brief: Planning permission has been granted for a single traveller pitch on agricultural land in the Ely area. The decision was reached despite formal concerns raised by the local council regarding the site. The approval allows for the development of the pitch on the designated plot, notwithstanding the objections previously put forward by planning officials.

stories.headline: School and parents exchange letters following protest
stories.brief: School leaders and parents have been exchanging letters following a recent protest. The correspondence comes as officials work to minimise any disruption to the upcoming exam season. No further details regarding the nature of the protest or the specific school involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Campaign launched against East Cambridgeshire wind farm proposals
stories.brief: A new campaign has been established to oppose plans for two wind farms in East Cambridgeshire. The proposed developments are located on Grade 1 agricultural land. Further details regarding the specific locations or the groups involved in the opposition have not yet been released.

stories.headline: New Police Community Support Officer joins Wisbech team
stories.brief:
A new Police Community Support Officer has joined the neighbourhood policing team in Wisbech. Jamie Gray-Esson has begun his role following the completion of his training. Since starting, he has been involved in several arrests following foot chases and has assisted colleagues with various crime enquiries.

Officer Gray-Esson has also been conducting patrols across local towns and villages, where he has engaged with shop staff, stallholders, and homeless individuals. In Wisbech town centre, he has been issuing parking tickets, with activity focused on Hill Street, Union Street, High Street, and East Place. The local policing team is encouraging residents to say hello if they see him out on patrol.

stories.headline: Recent cases heard at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court
stories.brief:
Several individuals appeared before King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court last week to face a variety of charges. Among those appearing were Natasha Faulkner of Downham, who will be sentenced on December 1 for failing to provide a breath test, and Geoffrey Ruskin of West Winch, who pleaded guilty to drink-driving after recording a breath alcohol reading three times the legal limit.

In other cases, Morgan Dowd of King’s Lynn pleaded guilty to harassment and using threatening behaviour, while Martin Gardner received a suspended prison sentence for breaching a non-molestation order. Additionally, an arrest warrant has been issued for Danny Clark of King’s Lynn, who is accused of shoplifting from a local store.

stories.headline: Wisbech man jailed following fuel station incident
stories.brief:
A 27-year-old man has been sentenced to six months in prison following an incident at a Wisbech filling station last October. Lewis Marsh, of no known address, was found guilty at Peterborough Magistrates' Court of racially aggravated criminal damage, using abusive words, and possessing a knife in public.

The court heard that Marsh entered the Lynn Road premises on October 8th, where he directed racist abuse at staff. He subsequently used a knife to slash the tyres of a van parked at the site. Marsh was arrested three days later on Duke Street. Police have described the incident as unprovoked and unacceptable behaviour.

stories.headline: Free flower seeds available in Peterborough
stories.brief: Residents in Peterborough are being offered free packets of flower seeds as part of the Seeds of Friendship project. The initiative aims to encourage local planting and community engagement through the distribution of these floral supplies. Those interested in taking part can collect the seeds to help brighten up their gardens and local spaces. Further details regarding the project and how to obtain the packets are available through the Seeds of Friendship scheme.

stories.headline: Potential housing for asylum seekers in Fenland
stories.brief: Reports suggest that Fenland could potentially accommodate up to 200 asylum seekers. The information, which originated from BBC coverage, is currently being discussed regarding the local area. No further details have been confirmed at this stage regarding specific locations or timelines for such a proposal. Residents are advised to stay tuned to Fenland Angels Radio for any further updates as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: Nearly 1,000 gather in Leverington to protest asylum seeker housing plans
stories.brief:
Nearly 1,000 people gathered outside Roman Court in Leverington on Sunday to protest against government plans to house asylum seekers at the site. This marks the second consecutive weekend of demonstrations against the proposal, which aims to accommodate 26 women and children as part of a wider plan for 205 asylum seekers in Fenland.

The district council and MP Steve Barclay have formally opposed the move, citing concerns over public safety, community cohesion, and the building's condition following an asbestos-related prohibition notice. A final decision on the use of the premises is expected from the government by Friday, October 16.

stories.headline: Norfolk police report 41 arrests in week-long road operation
stories.brief:
Norfolk Constabulary has concluded a week-long operation targeting criminal activity on the county’s road network. Known as Operation Lockstream, the initiative saw officers focus on major routes, including the A47 near Wisbech and at Swaffham. 

In total, 41 people were arrested and 40 vehicles were seized. Those detained face a variety of charges, including theft, drug offences, and immigration breaches. One stop led to the discovery of a cannabis cultivation site containing approximately 200 plants. Sergeant Josh Preston stated the operation used intelligence-led tactics to disrupt organised crime and improve road safety. The force confirmed the activity is part of ongoing efforts to prevent offenders from using local roads to facilitate criminal acts.

stories.headline: New planning applications submitted to Fenland District Council
stories.brief:
Fenland District Council has received a series of new planning applications across the region. Proposals include residential extensions at Euximoor Drove, Laddus Drove, and Church Lane, alongside plans for a new dwelling at Black Dyke. Commercial applications include the installation of electric vehicle charging stations at Belgrave Retail Park and a change of use for the Sunset Rooms on Station Road.

Several tree-related works have also been submitted, including requests to fell protected trees at the Village Pond and Village Green. Residents can view the full list of applications, including details on barn conversions and listed building alterations, by visiting the Fenland District Council planning portal.

stories.headline: Police appeal after motorbikes damage King’s Lynn football pitches
stories.brief:
West Norfolk Police are appealing for witnesses after football pitches at Lynnsport were damaged on Sunday evening. Officers report that a group of people on motorbikes, potentially including illegally modified e-bikes, gathered on the fields near Beulah Street at approximately 5pm. The activity left deep grooves in the playing surface.

Authorities are keen to identify those involved and are asking anyone with information to come forward. You can contact West Norfolk Police on 101, quoting reference number 36/76828/26. Alternatively, information can be provided anonymously by calling Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

stories.headline: Plans submitted for 80 new homes on historic site
stories.brief: A proposal has been put forward to construct 80 new homes on a site containing a Bronze Age burial ground. The development plans, reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, involve land currently known to hold archaeological remains from the Bronze Age period. No further details regarding the timeline or the status of the planning application have been provided at this stage. Residents are advised to monitor local planning portals for any updates concerning the potential impact on the site.

stories.headline: Financial support available for Long Sutton and Sutton Bridge students
stories.brief: Students living in Long Sutton and Sutton Bridge may be eligible for annual financial support of up to £400. Details regarding the potential funding have been reported by the Spalding South Holland News. Residents in these areas are encouraged to look into the criteria for this assistance.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire man convicted of attempted murder
stories.brief: A Cambridgeshire man has been found guilty of attempting to kill his partner. The court heard that the defendant carried out a violent attack against the woman, which involved both stabbing and electrocution. The case was reported by the Cambs Times.

stories.headline: Wisbech farm prepares for record-breaking pumpkin harvest
stories.brief:
A family-run farm in Wisbech is expecting its busiest Halloween season to date. Fen Farming, which has operated in the area for nearly 40 years, is set to supply over 500,000 pumpkins to Aldi stores nationwide. 

Despite a dry summer, the farm’s silt soil and new irrigation techniques have helped protect the crop across their 800-acre site. The business has invested over £750,000 in new harvesting and washing technology to meet the rising demand. Fen Farming has been a partner of the supermarket chain since 2014, growing from an initial supply of 25,000 squashes to becoming the retailer's largest pumpkin supplier.

stories.headline: Improvements completed at historic North Lynn pond
stories.brief:
Work has been carried out to restore the Long Pond off Loke Road in North Lynn following concerns raised by local residents. The site has been cleaned and refilled after reports that water levels had dropped significantly. 

County councillor Ben Griffin and borough councillor Austen Moore brought the matter to West Norfolk Council, which subsequently completed the maintenance. Councillor Griffin described the project as a positive step for the historic site, which dates back to the Civil War. Officials are now hoping this work will lead to further enhancements, ensuring the area remains a well-maintained space for the community to enjoy.

stories.headline: Police investigate altercation between two women in Fenland
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Police have launched an investigation following a fight involving two women in a Fenland town. Officers are currently looking into the circumstances surrounding the incident. No further details regarding the exact location or the condition of those involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: March business identifies barriers for black entrepreneurs
stories.brief: A company based in March has highlighted significant challenges facing black business owners. According to the firm, known as Rayo, a lack of belief is currently acting as a primary barrier holding back black entrepreneurs. The business shared these insights regarding the obstacles encountered by black-owned enterprises in the current economic climate.

stories.headline: GCSE results day in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Students across East Cambridgeshire are receiving their GCSE results today. The Ely Standard is providing live coverage as pupils collect their grades across the region. Families and students are encouraged to check local updates for the latest information regarding this year's examination outcomes.

stories.headline: Police appeal for help identifying three men following supermarket theft
stories.brief: Police are asking for the public’s assistance as they investigate a theft at a supermarket. Officers are working to identify three men in connection with the incident. Anyone who may have information that could assist the investigation is encouraged to come forward.

stories.headline: Police appeal following Peterborough collision
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Constabulary has issued an appeal for information following a road traffic collision in Peterborough. Officers are currently seeking witnesses or anyone with relevant details regarding the incident. Those who may have information are encouraged to contact the police force directly to assist with their ongoing enquiries.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire man admits to £126,000 fraud
stories.brief: A man from Cambridgeshire has entered a guilty plea for defrauding a woman out of £126,000. The case was reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News. No further details regarding the sentencing or the identity of the individual have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Obituary published for Norman Parnell
stories.brief: An obituary has been published for Norman Parnell, a resident of the Fenland area in Lincolnshire. The notice, which appeared in the Fenland Citizen, commemorates the life of Mr. Parnell in 2026. No further details regarding his life or funeral arrangements have been provided in the report.

stories.headline: Kitten rescued in Chatteris
stories.brief: A kitten has been rescued in Chatteris following an incident described as resembling a prison escape attempt. The young cat was recovered after an abseil-style rescue operation. No further details regarding the circumstances of the rescue or the current condition of the animal have been released.

stories.headline: Police investigation underway following reported school assault
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Police are currently investigating an alleged assault involving a pupil at a school in the county. Officers have provided an update on the situation, though specific details regarding the location of the school or the identity of those involved have not been released at this time. Authorities are continuing their inquiries into the incident.

stories.headline: Positive coronavirus tests confirmed at Lincolnshire school
stories.brief: A school in Lincolnshire has reported a number of positive coronavirus cases among its community. The news was confirmed by the institution following reports from local media outlets. Officials have not specified the exact number of individuals affected or identified the school involved. Parents and guardians are advised to monitor local updates for any further guidance regarding school operations or health protocols in the coming days.

stories.headline: Peterborough hosts AEPG Great Eastern Run
stories.brief: The AEPG Great Eastern Run has taken place in Peterborough. The half-marathon event saw participants take to the streets for the annual race. Following the conclusion of the competition, the Peterborough Telegraph has published a gallery featuring sixty photographs from the day’s proceedings. Residents and participants can view the images on the newspaper's website to see highlights from the course.

stories.headline: Liberal Democrats report high water leak levels in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: The Liberal Democrats have claimed that water leaks across Cambridgeshire are resulting in a significant loss of resources. According to the party, the volume of water escaping from the network is equivalent to filling 86 Olympic-sized swimming pools every single day. The figures were highlighted in a recent report by the Ely Standard.

stories.headline: Prison sentence for Christmas Day arsonist
stories.brief: A person has been jailed following an arson incident that took place on Christmas Day. Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed the sentencing today. No further details regarding the location of the fire or the identity of the individual have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Looking back at West Norfolk headlines from 1994
stories.brief:
We are looking back at the stories making headlines in West Norfolk during 1994. Plans for a two-million-pound science and technology block at Norfolk College in King’s Lynn were sent back to the drawing board after planners refused to allow protected trees to be removed. Meanwhile, the St Augustine’s Sports and Social Club in North Lynn celebrated its 21st birthday with a party for 350 members. 

Elsewhere that year, Fakenham councillors raised concerns over the relocation of the town’s post office, while Lynnsport hosted a major careers convention. Additionally, Middleton Village Hall announced early plans for VE-Day anniversary celebrations, and the local NHS trust reported that hospital waiting times had been successfully reduced.

stories.headline: Robbie Savage begins tenure at Peterborough
stories.brief: Robbie Savage has enjoyed a successful opening to his time at Peterborough. Reports indicate that the former footballer has secured a positive result in his first outing with the club. Further details regarding the specific match or his new role have not been disclosed at this stage.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire business leader named Deputy Lieutenant
stories.brief: A prominent business leader from Cambridgeshire has been appointed as a Deputy Lieutenant. The role has been awarded in recognition of their service to the local community.

stories.headline: Long-term future secured for Long Sutton Market House
stories.brief: Lincolnshire County Council has announced that the long-term future of the Market House in Long Sutton has been secured. The local authority confirmed the news regarding the historic site, though no further details on the specific plans or arrangements for the building have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Investigation launched following alleged assault at Cambridgeshire school
stories.brief: An investigation is underway following reports that a boy was assaulted at a school in Cambridgeshire. Details regarding the incident remain limited, but authorities have confirmed that inquiries into the matter have been launched. No further information has been released by officials at this stage.

stories.headline: Road closures announced across Cambridgeshire this week
stories.brief: Motorists travelling across Cambridgeshire are being advised to plan their journeys carefully as a series of road closures are in place this week. According to reports from the Ely Standard, several routes across the county will be affected by ongoing maintenance and improvement works. Drivers are encouraged to check their specific routes before setting off to avoid potential delays. Local authorities have not provided a full list of the affected roads, so commuters should remain alert for local signage and diversions while travelling through the region.

stories.headline: Calls for long-term solutions to antisocial behaviour in Lincolnshire
stories.brief: There are renewed calls for authorities to implement long-term strategies to tackle antisocial behaviour across Lincolnshire. The appeal, reported by the BBC, highlights a need for sustainable solutions to address ongoing concerns regarding public conduct within the county. Local officials and community representatives are being urged to look beyond short-term measures to ensure lasting improvements for residents. No specific locations or further details regarding the proposed plans have been provided at this stage.
